mappings.reason: Same legal person: Temasek Holdings (Private) Limited — identical label; b3 and b7 each hold it through wholly-owned vehicles (Dunearn; MacRitchie — Camas Investments is kept as its own node, see refusedMerges). No inventory id; each id was used by one file, so the first file's id (holders-b3.json) survives. Aliases, facts and sources unioned.

Same group: the Adani Group (Ahmedabad) — narratives-literature.json already uses grp:adani. Both are inventory ids (Atlas `adani`, national `grp:adani`); the energy fleet's reconciliation mapped adani → grp:adani, and the record's own type is a group. Alias "Adani Family" dropped (a family is not an alias of an institution).

The record is Reliance Industries Ltd the listed company (NSE: RELIANCE, parent of Jio Platforms, CMD Mukesh Ambani) — the national inventory id co:reliance-industries, which the holders files use for the same company. Same mapping as the energy fleet. Not grp:reliance (the promoter group) and not ADAG (energy:reliance-adag, cap:reliance-capital).

The record is the Tata Group (Tata Sons and subsidiaries — Talace, Tata Steel Long Products), ty group; the inventory has grp:tata (group) beside the Atlas company-typed `tata`. The group id matches the record's type and the energy fleet's adani → grp:adani precedent.

cross-fleet reconciliation 2026-09-26: same institution (Open Society Foundations — the Soros-founded grant-making network; both records: same label, same OCCRP/Munich facts, identity by the US entities' EINs in the ngo record). The ngo fleet owns foreign donors (contract: ngo:<slug> for associations and donors) and its record is the fuller one (IRS 990-PF figures, FCRA prior-reference, ED searches, contra). Capital's aliases, facts and sources were folded into ngo/donors-narratives.json; narratives-literature.json keeps a minimal copy because c015, c018 and c019 need the endpoint.
cross-fleet reconciliation 2026-09-26: same party; party:inc is the id defined by the welfare and ngo fleets (see energy/RECONCILIATION.json). Capital's record keeps its content under the new id.

cross-fleet reconciliation 2026-09-26: A court is not an energy/welfare entity; the Atlas holds the courts (sc, and from 2026-09-26 delhi-hc, bombay-hc, madras-hc, allahabad-hc, ap-hc, jharkhand-hc, sikkim-hc — ty agency, fam enforce, st of the seat). Facts and sources of the fleet record were copied into the Atlas node in src/graph/data.ts; the fleet file keeps its record under the Atlas id (the Atlas record wins in the merged graph). Id rewrite only. Referenced from rules-regulators.json c029 (no local record).

refusedMerges.reason: Both are Singapore state-owned investors, but Temasek Holdings (Private) Limited (investment company owned by the Minister for Finance) and GIC Private Limited (manager of Singapore's foreign reserves) are separate legal persons with separate holding vehicles in the filings (Dunearn/MacRitchie, and Camas at reported, vs "Government of Singapore"/GIC lines). Same sovereign, not the same entity.

MAS (the central bank, named on its own line in Shriram Finance, holders-b7:c009) and GIC (the reserve manager) are separate statutory/corporate bodies; merging would double-count Singapore lines in the same filing.
Separate bodies (investment company vs central bank); name of the state only.

Maggi Enterprises Ltd is a Nestlé promoter-group company filed on its own Table II line (28.48%, holders-b6:c007) beside Nestlé S.A. (34.28%, c006). Parentage is not identity, and no record in the file says it is a pure holding vehicle; kept separate as Pastel (Singtel), ICIL and HCL Holdings are.

Morgan Guaranty Trust Company of New York is a historical JPMorgan entity, but the corporate succession to JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. is not documented in any record opened by this fleet; the two filings (Wipro, Hindalco) name them differently. Kept apart until a primary record ties them.
Citibank N.A. (New York) as Grasim's GDR depositary vs Citigroup Global Markets India (LIC IPO book-runner, mandates-ventures:c015): different legal entities and roles in the same group.
Reliance Industries (Mukesh Ambani) vs Reliance Capital (Anil Dhirubhai Ambani Group, energy:reliance-adag lineage): separate groups since 2005; same name only.

Nippon Life India AMC was "Reliance Nippon Life AMC" under Reliance Capital (ADAG), never under Reliance Industries; the alias "Reliance Nippon Life Asset Management" stays on cap:nippon-india-amc only.
Parent (Japanese insurer, 75% after 2019, mandates-ventures:c041) and its Indian listed AMC — joined by an own edge, not the same entity.
A 50:50 joint venture is not its partner: BlackRock and Jio Financial Services each own half (mandates-ventures:c028/c029, holders:c019).
DSP BlackRock Investment Managers was a 60:40 JV until BlackRock sold its 40% in 2018 (mandates-ventures:c027); the former name "DSP BlackRock" stays an alias of cap:dsp-group.
Two JVs with separate SEBI registrations (MF investment manager, 26 May 2025; investment adviser INA000020314, 10 Jun 2025).
Separate companies with separate SEBI registrations (adviser vs stock-broker/clearing member).
Parent (Rothschild & Co SCA, Euronext: ROTH) and its Indian advisory subsidiary (CIN U65990MH1998PTC116788) — joined by own edges narratives-literature:c025 / mandates-ventures:c047.
Group vs its listed flagship company (inventory ids of different type).

The cluster node is 11 separately registered foreign promoter-group companies disclosed in Adani Enterprises / Adani Ports filings; the group is not its offshore shareholders, and folding them in would hide the ≥5% vehicles the critic asked to surface.
International Holding Company PJSC (ADX-listed conglomerate) and the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (sovereign fund) are different Abu Dhabi entities; the emirate is shared, identity is not.
A rule (the 2016–17 SEBI restrictions) vs the instrument it governs (narratives-literature:c028 is rule → instrument).
The 1982 convention (with its 2016 and 2024 protocols) vs the 2016 amending protocol recorded on its own in rules-regulators (c011). An amending instrument is not the treaty; both law nodes kept.
The Aug 2023 granular-disclosure circular and the Mar 2025 threshold increase are successive rules; the later one is recorded by date (rules-regulators:c019 ends 2025-03-24), not merged.
A committee the Supreme Court appointed is not the Court; merging would make the Court review itself.
A committee SEBI constituted to examine its own members' conflicts is kept apart from the regulator so its recommendations stay attributable.

Considered because both are Singapore state-linked: nothing on the record links Camas (UEN 200505776N) to GIC. Its only recorded parent link is to Temasek, via a registry aggregator, and that is kept as a reported-tier edge (holders-b3:c015), not a merge.

Second pass: the first pass's mapping cap:camas-investments → cap:temasek is undone (verifier: parent/vehicle, not a name-only merge, but an over-merge). Camas Investments Pte. Ltd. (Singapore UEN 200505776N) and Temasek Holdings (Private) Limited are separate legal persons; the parent link rests only on sgpbusiness.com, a registry aggregator, and the pre-edit holders-b4 record said Camas's owner was 'not asserted to be GIC, Temasek or any other named Singapore state entity'. Camas keeps its own node (full record holders-b4.json, minimal copy holders-b3.json) and its own documented holdings — holders-b3:c009 (Eternal 1.74%) and holders-b4:c003 (HDFC Life 1.68%), both back to tier documented because the filings name Camas itself — plus one own edge cap:temasek → cap:camas-investments at tier reported (holders-b3:c015, sgpbusiness.com). Dunearn and MacRitchie stay Temasek aliases (the fleet convention; MacRitchie's parentage is on a CCI order, Dunearn's on PitchBook, and holders-b3:c008 stays at reported).

Second pass: the first pass's mapping cap:pnotes-rules-2017 → cap:sebi-odi-circular-2017 is undone (verifier: a rule package rather than an entity). The SEBI board decision of 10 Jun 2016 (KYC and beneficial-owner identification for ODI subscribers) and the circular of 7 Jul 2017 (derivative-underlying ODIs barred, US$1,000 fee per subscriber) are separate regulatory acts. cap:pnotes-rules-2017 (rules-regulators.json, Angel One) records the 2016–17 package and cap:sebi-odi-circular-2017 (narratives-literature.json, Cyril Amarchand, Arthapedia) the 2017 circular; each keeps its own id, label, aliases, facts and sources as before the first pass. rules-regulators:c013 runs from cap:pnotes-rules-2017 again; narratives-literature:c028 stays on cap:sebi-odi-circular-2017; both are dated 2017-07-07 and neither is misattributed. The conflict over the beneficial-owner threshold (10% Angel One vs 25% Arthapedia) is kept as a gap on both records.

notes: Raw files were rewritten in place (ids, endpoints, benefit.who and prefixed ids in prose), so the mappings above are also a record for the assembler; none of the from-ids survives in any capital raw file.
AUDIT.json kills four further claims at assembly (mandates-ventures:c024, narratives-literature:c018, c022, rules-regulators:c010); they are not re-killed here.
Accusations by non-agencies (Hindenburg, OCCRP, BJP, INC) keep pred enforce with tier alleged — the fleet-wide encoding (energy/enforce.json does the same); the predicate vocabulary has no "accuses".
rules-regulators:c025 (sebi → law → its own conflict-of-interest committee) keeps pred law: no predicate in the vocabulary fits "constitutes a committee", and the edge is documented.

Holding vehicles named on filing lines (iShares funds, BAT's three vehicles, Temasek's Dunearn/MacRitchie, Sanlam's Mauritius vehicle) stay aliases of the parent — the fleet's convention; operating subsidiaries and listed companies (Jio Platforms, Tata Steel Long Products, Kotak IB, AIXL/AISATS, Bajaj Finserv AMC, Alphabet) were moved out of alias lists into d. Exception: Camas Investments Pte. Ltd. is kept as its own node with a reported own edge from Temasek, because its parent link rests only on a registry aggregator and its own batch record declined to name its owner (second pass).
Every alleged claim in the fleet already had a contra answering it by claim id in the same file; no contra had to be added. Every analytic claim carries an innocentReading.

cross-fleet reconciliation 2026-09-26: rules-regulators:c023, c024 (SC-appointed Expert Committee; Vishal Tiwari judgment) and c029 (Bombay HC stay in the Cals Refineries FIR matter) remain enforce claims from a court without the "Judicial ruling on <claim id>: " prefix — §4 warns — because the claim each rules on is not in rules-regulators.json (the Adani investigation lives in narratives-literature.json; the FIR order is not a claim anywhere). Left for the capital editor: either point them at claims in the file or move them.

undoneMappings.reason: Same registered company by identifier, not by name: holders-b4 records Camas Investments Pte. Ltd. with Singapore UEN 200505776N, and holders-b3 resolves the vehicle with the same UEN to Temasek (as an alias of cap:temasek). Vehicles are aliases of their parent throughout this fleet (Dunearn, MacRitchie, BAT's three vehicles, GIC). The parent link rests on a Singapore registry aggregator (sgpbusiness.com) — reported tier — so the claims routed through it are held at reported.

Same rule package: SEBI's 2016–17 tightening of P-Notes/ODIs (June 2016 board decision on KYC/UBO identification; circular of 7 Jul 2017 barring derivative-underlying ODIs, SIT on black money as the impetus). narratives-literature:c028 already describes the 2016–2017 package under cap:sebi-odi-circular-2017; rules-regulators:c013 cites the same 7 Jul 2017 circular. No inventory id; one file each; the first file's id survives, relabelled to cover both steps. The sources disagree on the UBO threshold (10% Angel One; 25% Arthapedia) — both kept in d.
